text: Over the next five years, sales grew about a quarter a year.
In 2014, a movie made of LEGO bricks earned close to half a billion dollars. In the first half of that year, LEGO passed Mattel and became the biggest toy company in the world.

So what nearly destroyed LEGO? Not one bad decision. A changing market pushed it to do more. Doing more filled its factories with pieces that were used once. The movies hid the cost. And when the movies stopped, the cost was all that was left.
The way out wasn't a new idea. It was the oldest one in the company. Fewer pieces, used again and again.
And through all of it, the copies, the losses, the movies, the rescue, one thing never changed. A LEGO brick made today... still clicks onto one made in 1958.
The bricks never stopped fitting together. For a few years, the company did.
